release.note: Library issue L126 records the gap as I raised it: a product with a subnormal float16 operand and a large partner sets the window, and num-dot Part 2 had no such input. Round 25 fixed it: DotF16 is now DotLiftAcc with relDot16 and absDot16, relative to |acc| + sum liftMag a * liftMag b, with evidence num-dot-sub16-round25. The prover re-proved the claim on it, and subnormal operands stay covered.

notes: Round 3 at gate 902c06ecf3fe60ae. work/Lift.lean prints the restated DotF16 (for all p, DotLiftAcc P <f16, f16, f32, p, 0> relDot16 absDot16), liftMag, minNormal8 (2^-14 for f16), dotLift and OutSpec with full names, and evaluates liftMag .f16 on 0, 3/4, -2^-14, 2^-24 and 1023*2^-24 (0, 3/4, 2^-14, 2^-14, 2^-14); the axioms are propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. DotLoop.stepRel, stepAbs and bound are unchanged, so rho, alpha, tol and every figure for normal operands are as before. On inputs made of subnormal-times-large products, the tolerance can exceed |S|: with all a = 2^-24, b = 65504 at K = 2^13, S = 31.98 and tol = 66.8. That is the shape of the library's fact, which the README states (a subnormal product counts up to 2^10 times its magnitude). Post still rejects a kernel that flushes subnormal inputs (a = 1023*2^-24, b = 1: S = 0.4995, bound 0.00126), and the host's torch.rand inputs add less than 2^-14 to A per subnormal operand.
